successors.name: Dutch East Indies
successors.text: northern South Sulawesi: the regencies of Luwu, North Luwu, East Luwu and Palopo City (infobox), the Gulf of Bone coast and foothills where Bugis settled round 1300

ledger.x: c. 1300: the Luwu kingdom is dated. Infobox 'Established ca. 1300'; 'Bugis settlers began to settle along the coastal margins of Luwu around the year 1300 CE'. The page also calls the 10th-14th century estimate from the La Galigo epic doubtful ('Estimated to be founded between the 10th and 14th century, but recent…

c. 1620: the capital moves from Malangke to Palopo. 'Around 1620, Malangke was abandoned and a new capital was established to the west at Palopo' (the page also cites the economic potential of trade with the Toraja highlands).
1905: Luwu ends as a sovereign kingdom (bridging, page silent).

wars.name: Dewaraja's attacks on Wajo and Sidenreng
wars.outcome: 'Stories current today in South Sulawesi tell of his aggressive attacks on the neighboring kingdoms of Wajo and Sidenreng' (Dewaraja, c.

certainty.note: The page gives no frontier for any date; the disc stands for the regencies of the infobox.
